title: Breadcrumb Filters: Fast Fully Featured Filters
bound_sents: This suggests the following open problem: For space-efficient filters, do you have to sacrifice performance to support enumerability? 1 Space efficiency of a filter is the ratio of its size and the information-theoretic lower bound, i.e. the space efficiency of a filter instance of size 𝑆 bits with  …
The numerator, 𝑛 log 𝜀 −1 , represents the information-theoretic minimum space required [17], while the denominator reflects the actual space used.
All the filter designs we consider (except the Bloom filter with 1.44𝑛 log 𝜀 −1 space usage) incur an overhead of Ω(𝑛) bits beyond the lower bound.
